analysis.title: What's next after the tech sell-off?
key_insights: The tech-led sell-off reflects two forces per Eastspring's Chief Economist Ray Farris: higher bond yields from global central bank tightening constraining AI infrastructure financing, and US mid-term results shifting control of local governments from AI-friendly Republicans to Democrats who favour more AI regulation. The Nasdaq fell 5.9% in the prior US session.

Eastspring expects delays to data center projects, not cancellations or outright mass prohibitions. None of the winning Democrats in the key states identified argues for a ban. Their platforms push for rules on local utility costs, changes to data center taxes, and local approval authority. Some have advocated temporary moratoria while legislation passes.

Neocloud planned spending is about 7% of estimated total US AI spending in 2027. If half of it were canceled, which Eastspring calls likely an overestimate, total spending would fall by only about USD84bn.

Hyperscalers account for about 93% of planned AI capex and do not appear financing constrained. Since October 1 they have raised USD199.9bn: USD72.5bn in bonds, USD12.5bn in mandatory convertibles, USD34.9bn in equity and USD80bn in supplier financing. Another USD60bn hyperscaler equity offering is in progress and likely to complete.
A leading AI lab is raising up to USD100bn in an IPO, and roughly USD35bn in neocloud IPOs are in progress.

Data center capacity is still in deficit relative to demand. Rental rates for new H100 and B200 racks are at new highs, rates for six-year-old A100 racks have reversed higher, and several US hyperscalers said in Q3 earnings that compute shortages limited their revenues.

Investment bank estimates for 2027-2030 global data center capacity additions rose from about 110GW to 180-230GW since mid-year. This drove upgrades to 2027 earnings estimates for Japan, Taiwan and Korea, and Eastspring says part of those upgrades are now at risk of cuts.

Most 2027 IT hardware revenue is already locked in. Per Alterio data, the US has 85GW of data centers under development across 888 facilities, with only about 8.4GW delayed. Most will proceed and need GPUs, DRAM and other hardware, mainly from Asian producers.

Alterio counts 464GW of pre-development data centers in the proposal stage, which Eastspring judges unlikely. It keeps its midyear base case of about 110GW of new compute through 2030, equal to about USD4.2tn at USD38.5bn per GW. Its bear case is about 75GW, or USD2.9tn.

Recent price falls have already discounted a good deal of earnings downgrade risk. Forward P/E ratios are well off the year's highs, and forward P/E-to-earnings-growth ratios are low enough that very large estimate cuts would be needed to return to average levels. Eastspring cannot rule out further de-rating.

Multi Asset Portfolio Solutions team sees it as premature to assume a sustained disruption to the AI cycle or US growth. It says volatility-targeting strategies and leveraged ETF deleveraging amplified the move.

The multi-asset team cut its equity overweight earlier this week after its systematic signals weakened and moved from overweight to underweight Emerging Markets relative to the US. It keeps a modest equity overweight and favours semiconductors, cybersecurity, Korea, European banks and long-duration assets.

The multi-asset team says further near-term weakness is possible as positioning adjusts. It will reassess adding equity exposure selectively, directly or through options, once markets show stabilisation.

Equities: performance is expected to become more differentiated as AI spending broadens from GPUs into memory, advanced packaging and networking. Asia tech managers are using the correction to find attractively valued companies with strong earnings growth.

Value managers were largely underweight tech/AI going into the sell-off, which helped. They are asking whether the valuation reset more than discounts the feared deterioration in growth or profitability.
India equities could be a compelling opportunity especially if energy prices fall. Recent underperformance reflects higher oil prices and limited participation in the AI rally.
Asia dividend investing: a diversified, style-agnostic approach across the dividend cycle is meant to be more resilient as market leadership rotates.

Bonds are regaining their defensive role as yields fall. The fixed income team is actively managing duration, emphasising credit quality and liquidity, and notes starting yields still provide meaningful carry and potential capital gains if growth risks intensify.

sector_views.rationale: Long-term AI opportunity intact and valuations adjusted, but the team stays cautious near term and expects more differentiated performance. Semiconductors and cybersecurity remain favoured structural exposures.
Favoured by the multi-asset team as a diversifying position.
Bonds are regaining their defensive role as yields fall, and starting yields are attractive.

earnings_insights: Part of the upward revisions to 2027 earnings estimates for Japan, Taiwan and Korea are at risk of downgrades, per Eastspring. Consensus 2027 earnings estimates for these markets rose significantly since mid-year.
Several US hyperscalers said in Q3 earnings announcements that compute shortages limited their revenues.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Tech-led sell-off ahead of and after the US mid-terms, amplified by volatility-targeting and leveraged ETF deleveraging.

macro_indicators.reading: about 110GW, about USD4.2tn at USD38.5bn per GW
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports continued hardware demand. Bank estimates of 180-230GW are seen as too high.

macro_indicators.indicator: Global data center capacity additions 2027-2030 (Eastspring bear case)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Even the bear case implies large hardware spending.

risk_factors: Higher bond yields from global central bank tightening could constrain AI infrastructure financing, crowding out some neocloud spending.
Tighter state-level data center regulation, including possible temporary moratoria, could delay projects.
Markets may further discount AI earnings downgrade risk, and 2027 earnings estimates for Japan, Taiwan and Korea could be cut.
Pre-development data center capacity in the proposal stage may not materialise.
Higher oil prices weigh on India equities.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers (about 93% of capex) raised USD199.9bn since October 1, compute capacity is in deficit, GPU rental rates are at new highs, and 85GW is already under development with most 2027 hardware revenue locked in.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher yields could crowd out neocloud spending, state regulation could delay projects, and 2027 earnings estimates built on 180-230GW capacity forecasts are at risk of downgrades.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further earnings downgrades or a sustained disruption to the AI investment cycle or US growth. The report names no specific level.
